newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU asks Japan to lift remaining market barriers.
newsitem.headline: EU asks Japan to lift remaining market barriers.

text.p: The European Commission asked Japan on Monday to make a "determined effort" to lift market barriers for products ranging from cars to race horses when it prepares a final round of deregulation measures next week.

"We will be looking for clear unequivocal commitments, along with a precise timetable for the implementation of measures across all sectors of the Japanese economy," Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said in a statement.
The Commission, which submitted 202 deregulation proposals to Japan last November, said Tokyo had made progress in areas including insurance, electrical equipment and cosmetics.

But many import barriers remained, it said, citing the certification system for cars and car parts, approval procedures for fresh fruit and vegetables, foreign ownership restrictions in the telecommunications sector and import licences for starch.

Furthermore, it said, Japan discriminates against foreign race horses. "At present, only 12 (out of a total of 27,000 races) will be open to foreign horses with overseas race experience by the year 1999," it said.
Japan is due to publish the final revision of a three-year deregulation programme at the end of March, the statement said.
